Two-variable (bivariate) choropleth map

Source: R/bivariate_choropleth_map.R
mysterymaps_bivariate_choropleth_map.Rd

Shades each polygon by the joint class of two numeric variables at once – e.g. population need versus provider scarcity – so a reader sees where the two overlap without needing two separate maps. Includes an n_classes x n_classes legend grid (terciles, n_classes = 3, by default) rendered as an inset, not a separate figure.

Usage

mysterymaps_bivariate_choropleth_map(
  polygons,
  x_var,
  y_var,
  x_label,
  y_label,
  title = NULL,
  subtitle = NULL,
  caption = NULL,
  palette = MYSTERYMAPS_BIVARIATE_PALETTE,
  na_color = "grey85",
  crs = 5070,
  legend_position = "br",
  legend_size = 0.16,
  n_classes = 3
)

Arguments

polygons

sf polygon layer.

x_var, y_var

character(1): numeric columns in polygons.

x_label, y_label

character(1): full-word axis labels for the legend grid (e.g. "Women Age 40 and Older", not "Women 40+").

title, subtitle, caption

Character labels. NULL omits.

palette

Named length-n_classes^2 colour vector, keys "1-1" .. "<n_classes>-<n_classes>" (x class first, y class second). Default MYSTERYMAPS_BIVARIATE_PALETTE when n_classes = 3 (its literal, hand-tuned values, not a regenerated approximation); auto-generated via bilinear interpolation of the same four corner colours for any other n_classes, unless a palette is supplied explicitly.

na_color

Colour for polygons missing x_var or y_var.

crs

Projection for display. Default EPSG:5070 (Albers Equal Area), appropriate for the contiguous United States.

legend_position

character(1): corner for the legend inset, one of "br", "bl", "tr", "tl". Default "br", which leaves the bottom-left corner free for mysterymaps_scale_bar().

legend_size

numeric(1): the inset's width and height, as a fraction of polygons' bounding-box width and height respectively. Default 0.16. A bounding-box CORNER is usually the part of an irregular shape (a coastline, a state outline) farthest from the shape itself, so a small inset tucked flush into one, as this is by default, generally lands in blank space rather than over the mapped area; shrink legend_size further for a shape where that isn't true, or pick a different legend_position.

n_classes

integer(1): classes per axis (so the legend is n_classes x n_classes). Default 3, the cartographic standard – human colour perception reliably resolves about 3 steps varying along two channels at once; above roughly 4, interpolated cells stop being reliably distinguishable from their neighbours. Must be >= 2.

Value

A ggplot object. The caller saves it; this function writes nothing.

Details

The legend inset is built with ggplot2::annotation_custom() around a small second ggplot, not cowplot::draw_plot(). This package does not depend on cowplot, and annotation_custom() does the same job – drawing one grob inside another plot's panel – without adding a dependency for it.

Each variable is split into n_classes groups independently with classInt::classIntervals() (style = "quantile"), so the bivariate class reflects each variable's own distribution rather than a shared arbitrary cutoff. A polygon with NA in either variable gets NA for the joint class and is drawn in na_color.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
counties <- sf::st_sf(
  rate = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9),
  need = c(9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1),
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(lapply(1:9, function(i) {
    x <- -100 + i
    sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(c(x, x + 1, x + 1, x, x), c(40, 40, 41, 41, 40))))
  }), crs = 4326)
)
mysterymaps_bivariate_choropleth_map(
  counties, x_var = "rate", y_var = "need",
  x_label = "Providers per Capita", y_label = "Population Need")
}
